name: Rucht

attributes.attribute: known as Finnbennach, the great bull
fought through rebirth as stags, ravens and worms
sought a bull equal to her husband's
died in the bull fight of the epic

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Rucht is an Irish hero who is little known under his human name. He is famous as Finnbennach, the white horn, the finest bull of Connacht. In the tale he began as a swineherd. He argued with a fellow swineherd named Friuch. Their quarrel ran so deep that, reborn over and over, they kept fighting, first as stags, then as ravens, and at last as worms. Two worms can do little harm, and the two were far apart on the island. This stage set up the next move. The first worm pressed the great queen Medb into marrying Ailill, and the second warned Dáire that Medb might invade Ulster. Then cows ate the worms and bore them anew as bull calves. When the bulls grew up, Medb took offence because her husband owned Finnbennach and so stood above her in rank. She set seeking a bull that matched his. The only fit animal was Rucht's old rival, who by then wore the form of that brown bull, Donn Cuailnge. Their fight is the subject of the great Irish epic Táin Bó Cuailnge. Brought together at last, the old rivals fell to fighting once more. Rucht was killed and his bull body scattered in pieces over the land. His rival did not outlive the win for long, dying of weariness and loss of blood on the way home.

okr.objective: Present Rucht as the hero reborn as the bull Finnbennach at the heart of the Irish epic.
key_results: Little is known of his human name.
He is famed as Finnbennach, the great bull of Connacht.
He fought his rival in many reborn forms.
The bull fight gives the epic Táin Bó Cuailnge its core.
